components.gap: Define, in the owned 166.1 text, the event/probability-vector domain of the discrete entropy functional H(p)=-K sum p_i log p_i (finite vectors, and the countable case where H may be +infinity), its logarithmic unit as the free positive constant/base with the justified rescaling H_b=H/ln b between nats and bits, and the 0 log 0 convention; the route has only scattered auxiliary definitions in other chapters (finite alphabet in nats, base-two vectors, bits-to-nats remark) and no unified definition on the actual domain.

evidence.label: thm:p15-rmdl-dependence (sum of marginal entropies minus joint = divergence>=0)

components.gap: Supply Shannon's characterization theorem (continuity in p, monotone increase of the uniform value in n, and the grouping/decomposition property imply H=-K sum p log p) with the full Appendix 2 proof written out, and the finite joint/conditional properties with full proofs: H(x,y)<=H(x)+H(y) with equality iff independence, the definition of conditional entropy H_x(y), the chain rule H(x,y)=H(x)+H_x(y), H_x(y)<=H(y) with equality iff independence, and the equalizing-change (averaging) increase of H; at present only the uniform maximum, a base-two subadditivity identity for innovations and one expected-information identity appear, and the characterization is absent.

Present the selected continuous-entropy properties of Shannon Section 20 with integrability assumptions (existence of -int p log p, possibility of -infinity/undefined values) and proofs: dependence on the coordinate system with the change-of-variables formula h(y)=h(x)-E log|J| (Jacobian of the transformation), the linear case adding log|det a|, invariance under measure-preserving maps, the bounded-volume and fixed-variance maximizers, h(x,y)<=h(x)+h(y) and h_x(y)<=h(y), and the coordinate invariance of differences such as h(x)-h_y(x); the route has only a one-chapter differential-entropy definition and one bounded-interval maximum-entropy theorem, with coordinate dependence asserted in one sentence without a formula or proof.

State in the entropy method, with a worked contrast, that entropy measures the statistical amount of information of a distribution and is neither semantic truth (Shannon's semantic-irrelevance stipulation), nor evidential support for a hypothesis, nor decision value/utility, computing the named quantities for one example in which a high-entropy description is false or decision-irrelevant; only isolated disclaimers in other chapters exist.
